text:
Priya Rao: Quick follow-up on the RFC for fallback where Private sidecars can be quarantined and traffic routed to Hosted/Dedicated. See RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/priv-quarantine (summary below)
Priya Rao: TL;DR: we need a safe plan to evacuate a compromised private-sidecar tenant to Hosted/Dedicated without exposing long-lived customer creds or expanding blast radius.
Devon Li: Quick Q: on credential handling — do we rebind tenant creds to hosted runtime or use an exchange/ephemeral proxy? Rebind feels dangerous.
Samir Patel: Strong +1 on ephemeral. Proposal: token-exchange flow where the control plane mints a short-lived exchange token (audience=hosted, ttl=60s, scope=inference-only). Hosted runtime redeems it and gets a scoped ephemeral session. No customer keys copied.
Anya Kuznetsova: Observability concerns: we must attach a quarantine tag to spans and logs so we can filter/aggregate without leaking tenant identifiers. Suggest span tag: `quarantine=true` and `tenant_hash=<sha256prefix>` for safe correlation.
Priya Rao: Rollout plan suggestion: feature flag at tenant level -> canary (10 tenants) -> 1% traffic sweep -> escalate. Metrics: error-rate, p95 latency delta, cost-per-token. Abort criteria: error-rate >5% sustained over 5m or p95 > 1.5x baseline.
Devon Li: Circuit breaker semantics: if hosted can't use identical model variant, route to a compatible fallback variant and set response header `x-rdwd-fallback=1`. Console should show which variant served.
Samir Patel: Ops/billing: quarantine will move work to Hosted/Dedicated; potential cost spike. Add billing alert rule and tag quarantine flows with `quarantine.tenant=<id>` so we can attribute cost.
Anya Kuznetsova: Tests: add e2e harness cases for 1) sidecar network egress blocked 2) secret rotation while quarantined 3) KMS outage during token minting. Run in infra-ci and nightly.
Priya Rao: Security note (important): do NOT copy or escrow customer-managed keys into Hosted. Use an exchange/DST pattern and HSM-signed ephemeral tokens. All audit events MUST include an obfuscated tenant id and exchange reason.
Devon Li: Implementation TODOs (short list):
  1) token-exchange endpoint + schema
  2) audit-event schema + retention policy
  3) console feature flag UI + visibility of fallback variant
  4) runbook + rollback playbook
Samir Patel: I'll own audit events + cost tagging. Need simple schema: `event_type=quarantine_exchange`, `tenant_hash`, `actor=controlplane`, `outcome=redeem_success|redeem_fail`. Keep as plaintext in event store but encrypted at rest.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for feature/priv-fallback -> build 9934 -> staged in infra-canary -> watch metrics -> link: https://ci.redwood/internal/9934
Priya Rao: Runbook snippet for oncall:
```
If errors >5% -> toggle ff=off -> call `quarantine.invalidate(<tenant>)` -> open P0 and page security + infra
If hosted token minting failing -> fail closed (do not issue long-lived fallbacks) -> route back to private with 429 + meta explaining degraded state
If cost > $X/min -> throttle quarantined tenants and contact account owner
```
Samir Patel: Also: ensure we surface `quarantine` events to the compliance audit stream (immutable) and to customer-facing audit export when requested.
Anya Kuznetsova: One more SLO item: p95 latency for quarantined requests must not exceed 1.5x normal; if it does, prefer returning a graceful degrade (short answer + reason) instead of a high-latency full response. Add a dedicated alert for that.
Priya Rao: Postmortem template addendum: include `leakage-checklist` (verify no secret persisted in hosted logs), `audit-log-diff`, and `cost-impact` section.
Devon Li: I'll pick up token-exchange endpoint and create an initial PR with schema + integration tests.
Samir Patel: I'll wire audit events, cost tags, and the billing alert.
Anya Kuznetsova: I'll add tracing keys, the `quarantine` span tag, and the e2e tests in infra-ci.
Priya Rao: I'll draft the RFC follow-up doc with runbook, rollout steps, and owner assignments and file it by EOD. Assigning action owners here in thread.
Devon Li: One open tradeoff: do we allow hosted to serve using quantized variants producing slightly different outputs? That may be necessary to meet latency but could cause quality regression. Need eval harness to gate by semantic-similarity threshold.
Samir Patel: Agree — add a gating eval: fallback allowed if semantic-similarity >= 0.92 on tenant prompt set. If below, prefer fail-back to private or return degrade message.
Priya Rao: Great. I'll include that gating criteria in the RFC follow-up. Thanks all :thumbsup:
